description: Robot capabilities that teams demonstrate or deploy now, mapped to task families, site types and per-source selectors. The builder enumerates the union of site types of active rows. Adding a row or a site type is a data change.

selector_rules.naics: A code matches the site type with the longest matching prefix, unless an exclude prefix matches. OSHA ITA and EPA FRS use naics_prefixes.
selector_rules.sic: Same longest-prefix rule for 1987 SIC codes. EPA FRS uses sic_prefixes only for a facility that has no NAICS code.
selector_rules.osm: Each selector is a tag map; a value list means any of the values. Every Overpass query also requires a name tag. A generic site type applies only when no other site type matched. A match on an exclusion site type drops the OpenStreetMap feature. name_excludes drops OpenStreetMap features of that site type whose normalized name contains one of the phrases.
selector_rules.fsis_mpi: all_establishments: every establishment in the FSIS Meat, Poultry and Egg Product Inspection Directory.

rows.label: Fixed-arm CNC and molding machine tending

evidence.claim: Formic installed a Formic Tend cell with a 6-axis FANUC arm to load and unload injection molding machines at ICON Injection Molding in Phoenix, Arizona, and reported a 20% production increase.
Tool Gauge in Tacoma, Washington uses Universal Robots cobots for CNC machine tending and glue dispensing.
Whippany Actuation Systems, an aerospace manufacturer in New Jersey, uses a UR10 cobot to tend CNC machines during unattended overnight shifts.
Integrator AEC built a FANUC CRX cell on a Vention 7th axis that tends CNC machine tools, a CMM and part marking for a cast-parts maker in Greer, South Carolina.

rows.label: Part kitting, sequencing and fixture loading

evidence.claim: Figure says its F.02 humanoids loaded more than 90,000 sheet-metal parts onto welding fixtures on an active BMW Spartanburg line over an 11-month deployment.
Figure says F.03 started parts sequencing in Hall 52 at BMW Plant Spartanburg, placing parts that arrive in different orientations into the correct slots for the line.
Apptronik's commercial agreement with Mercedes-Benz covers a pilot of Apollo delivering assembly kits to the line and delivering totes of kitted parts.
Boston Dynamics opened a training center at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America near Savannah, Georgia, where Atlas is trained to sequence automotive parts before assembly.

rows.label: Case, tote and each picking in warehouses

evidence.claim: Agility says Digit has moved more than 100,000 totes at GXO's Flowery Branch, Georgia facility, moving totes between AMRs and conveyors.
Agility and Mercado Libre agreed to deploy Digit for commerce fulfillment tasks at Mercado Libre's facility in San Antonio, Texas.
The Feed installed 48 Brightpick Autopickers at its Colorado facility; the robots take storage totes from shelving and pick items into order totes.
Brightpick reports 103 Autopickers running around the clock at an e-commerce DC near Denver, Colorado.
DHL signed an MoU for more than 1,000 additional Boston Dynamics Stretch robots by 2030; Stretch unloads containers and trailers in DHL's North American operations.
UPS plans to spend about $120 million on 400 Pickle Robot truck-unloading robots across multiple facilities from the second half of 2026.
FedEx and Berkshire Grey unveiled Scoop, an autonomous trailer unloader in pilot, with the first systems expected later in 2026.

rows.label: Mixed-case palletizing and depalletizing

evidence.claim: After a pilot in Brooksville, Florida, Walmart agreed to install Symbotic's system, which includes palletizing robots, in 25 more regional DCs.
Plus One Robotics put mixed-case depalletizing systems into service at a FedEx facility in Reno, Nevada.
Jacobi Robotics and Delta Technology commissioned a FANUC cell that does random mixed-case palletizing for a manufacturer's parcel fulfillment.
Napco Brands, a coffee packer in the Chicago area, runs two Universal Robots cobot palletizing cells at the end of its packing lines.

rows.notes: No verified mixed-case palletizing deployment in a food or beverage plant; the food-plant evidence is single-SKU end-of-line palletizing.

rows.label: Parcel sorting, induction and piece picking

evidence.claim: Figure showed Helix-controlled humanoids moving packages between conveyors and turning them so the label faces the scanner.
OSM Worldwide deployed AmbiSort systems that sort mixed parcels into mailsacks at its Atlanta, Chicago and Las Vegas warehouses.
After a pilot at its Bloomington, California hub, Pitney Bowes said it would deploy Ambi parcel-sorting robots across its US e-commerce hubs.
FedEx installed Plus One and Yaskawa robotic arms at its Memphis World Hub to induct small parcels into high-speed sorters.

rows.label: AI robotic sorting at materials recovery facilities

evidence.claim: The Kent County, Michigan Recycling & Education Center runs three AMP AI robots that sort plastics on its lines.
Waste Connections agreed to deploy 24 AMP AI-guided sorting robots on container, fiber and residue lines across its MRFs.
Glacier announced a fleet of AI sorting robots at Recology's King County MRF in Seattle.
Lakeshore Recycling Systems installed an EverestLabs robot on the residue line of a Chicago MRF to recover aluminum cans.

rows.label: Sorting at scrap and recyclable material yards
rows.notes: No verified robot deployment at a scrap yard or recyclable material wholesaler yet.

rows.label: Bimanual towel, linen and garment folding

evidence.claim: Figure showed a Helix-controlled humanoid autonomously folding towels picked from a mixed pile.
Dyna Robotics reported that DYNA-1 folded more than 800 napkins in a continuous 24-hour autonomous run.
Monster Laundry in Sacramento, California runs a Dyna Robotics folding system that folds towels, linens and clothing.
In a San Francisco laundry room, a Weave Robotics robot folds part of the items for Tumble's wash-and-fold service.

rows.notes: Verified deployments are laundromat and wash-and-fold sites plus lab demos; no verified US industrial linen-plant deployment yet. NAICS 812320 also includes small retail dry cleaners.

rows.label: Food assembly and handling on production lines

evidence.claim: Chef Robotics robots put ingredients into frozen-meal bowls on Amy's Kitchen production lines.
Chef Robotics' AI arms place ingredients into trays on meal-assembly lines for food manufacturers including Amy's Kitchen and Sunbasket.

rows.label: Food preparation in commercial kitchens

evidence.claim: White Castle agreed to install Miso Robotics' Flippy 2 fry-station robot at 100 restaurants.
Miso began piloting its next-generation Flippy Fry Station at White Castle in late 2024 and scheduled rollouts to other brands.

rows.notes: Verified evidence is restaurant fry stations; NAICS 7223 covers contractors and caterers, not restaurants.

rows.label: Store shelf restocking and backroom replenishment

evidence.claim: Telexistence announced deployment of TX SCARA robots that restock refrigerated beverage shelves in 300 FamilyMart stores in Japan and said it plans to expand to US convenience stores.
Telexistence is piloting its TX Ghost beverage-restocking robot in the chilled backrooms of selected 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo.
Brain Corp showed Project Brawn, a prototype mobile manipulator for picking and stocking in stores; no named deployment.
Context only: Harmons rolled out Simbe's Tally shelf-scanning robot to 17 Utah grocery stores; it scans shelves and does not restock.

rows.notes: Active for the first build by owner direction. No verified US restocking deployment yet; verified deployments are Japanese convenience stores and a US prototype.

rows.label: Cooler restocking in convenience stores

evidence.claim: Telexistence announced deployment of TX SCARA robots that restock refrigerated beverage shelves in 300 FamilyMart stores in Japan and said it plans to expand to US convenience stores.
Telexistence is piloting its TX Ghost beverage-restocking robot in the chilled backrooms of selected 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo.

rows.notes: Left out of v1 to keep the first snapshot on large-format stores.

rows.label: Hospital delivery of supplies, specimens and medications

evidence.claim: Diligent Robotics said its Moxi fleet passed 1 million hospital deliveries of supplies, specimens and medications across US health systems.
Diligent began rolling out Moxi 2.0 to US health systems; Moxi works in more than 25 US hospitals.
BayCare added Relay robots at two Winter Haven, Florida hospitals to carry lab specimens, pharmacy orders and supplies.
Upstate Medical University in Syracuse, New York runs 14 Aethon TUG robots that deliver medicines, supplies, linens and meals.

rows.label: Autonomous floor cleaning

evidence.claim: Sam's Club put BrainOS-powered autonomous floor scrubbers in all of its roughly 600 US clubs.
Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport deployed Avidbots Neo autonomous floor scrubbers.
Brain Corp reported more than 37,000 BrainOS robots, with the fastest growth in warehouse and industrial sites.
Tennant launched the X16 Sweep, an autonomous sweeper for warehouses, logistics centers and light manufacturing.

rows.notes: Mature navigation-only category; it is not yet a Blueprint manipulation evaluation target.

rows.label: Sample and labware handling in laboratories

evidence.claim: PNNL's EMSL chose Ginkgo Automation to build an automated anaerobic phenotyping workcell on its modular cart system.
PNNL commissioned an autonomous lab where robots fill and load sample containers and move them between lab locations.
Medra raised a Series A for general-purpose robots that run lab experiments autonomously.
Automata raised $45M to scale its modular lab-robotics platform for pharma customers.

rows.notes: Verified evidence is research and pharma labs; no hospital clinical-lab deployment verified.

rows.label: Harvesting in greenhouses and indoor farms

evidence.claim: Oishii bought Tortuga AgTech's harvesting-robot IP and team; Oishii's indoor farm runs about 50 robots that check strawberry ripeness before picking.
Four Growers robots harvest tomatoes in Nature Fresh Farms' greenhouse in Leamington, Ontario.
Westburg Greenhouse in the Netherlands runs a fleet of Four Growers tomato-harvesting robots.
Four Growers, based in Pittsburgh, says its greenhouse harvesting robots work with five customers.

rows.notes: Verified deployments are in Canada, the Netherlands and one US indoor farm.

evidence.claim: Dream Hollywood in Los Angeles runs two Relay delivery robots that bring food, amenities and towels to guests.
Relay says its robots carry food and housekeeping supplies in hotels including Embassy Suites LAX North.
Luma Hotel in Times Square used Relay 2 robots to deliver linens, towels and food.
TechForce Robotics' TIM-E robot moves linen and waste bins for housekeeping at Homewood Suites in Del Mar, California.
